title: Basic credentials whose password contains a colon
summary: A synthetic Basic token whose decoded password itself contains a colon.
rationale: Only the first colon delimits user-id from password, so a second colon is part of the secret. Because the token is one encoded unit, the extent is unaffected in the source, but a consumer that decodes and splits on every colon would shorten the decoded password; that decoded mapping is downstream.

expectation.rationale: Flag, with the whole token as the extent. RFC 7617 says text after the first colon is part of the password.

sources.supports: the first colon in a user-pass string separates user-id and password from one another; text after the first colon is part of the password

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
